label: header

label: paragraph_title
text: STEAMBOAT

label: text
text: She is being "worked in" temporarily on the Macao run and we hope the general public will take the opportunity of visiting Macao whilst they can do so under the comfortable, not to say "luxurious conditions" which this vessel affords. She re-placed our old friend the "Honum" which after 43 years' very faithful service was sold for breaking up purposes last December. Her passing removes one of the oldest "landmarks" on the river and to the end, her machinery and engines were a tribute to the integrity and superiority of British engineering and shipbuilding.

label: text
text: We regret that owing to the present financial position of the company, the prevailing tightness of the money market coupled with the inadvisability of realising the company's holdings in local stocks at their present low level and which will doubtless commend itself to you, since they are first-class investments, they are unable to recommend the payment of any dividend this year. Our fleet has been further written down during the year and has, as usual, been maintained in good order and condition. It is futile, gentlemen, to speak of the future, and I can only close with the expression of sincere hope that before very long the present unfortunate disagreements between here and Canton, which for many months now have distinguished our former happy relations, will pass away and mutual trade once more resume its away between the two ports without which neither of us can hope to satisfactorily develop the great trading opportunities which await us both with the return of settled and peaceful conditions.

label: text
text: It would be ill-fitting for me to sit down without referring to the tragical death of our esteemed friend and colleague, Mr. Chau Sui-ki, whose untimely end distressed us all, and indeed the whole Colony. He was a most regular attendant at our board meetings and we were profoundly impressed with his sagacity and wide knowledge in handling the many problems which arise during the course of the year in handling such a company as this. To his surviving family, I tender on behalf of us all our sincerest sympathy in their great bereavement. To many of us gathered in this room he was an intimate personal friend whom we could ill afford to lose, and shall mourn for many a day.

label: text
text: I do not think I can usefully add more to what I have already said, gentlemen, and I now formally propose the adoption of the report and accounts as presented and after the motion has been seconded, I shall be pleased to answer any enquiries you may desire to put to me to the best of my ability.

label: paragraph_title
text: Policy Endorsed.

label: text
text: Mr. L. S. Greenhill said: It gives me much pleasure to second the adoption of the report and accounts as presented. After the interesting speech of the chairman, I think it quite unnecessary for me to make any other comments. Considering the conditions which have ruled during the last six months of our working year, I think all shareholders will join me in voicing our appreciation of the very satisfactory work done by our directors, our staff afloat and on shore under more than normally trying conditions.

label: text
text: With these few words I beg to second the adoption of the report and accounts as presented.

label: text

Disastrous Bush fires have also occurred in South Australia. Ten square miles of country were swept in the Mount Pleasant district. One owner lost 2,500 sheep.
The damage is estimated at £140,000.

Steel-Maitland, Minister of Labour, said that he refused to appoint a Commission of Enquiry into the marine wireless operators' dispute on the ground that such a Court could only be empowered to enquire in the circumstances and not lay down terms of settlement.

label: text
text: Rugby; Feb. 15.

label: text
text: Sir Arthur Steel-Maitland, Minister of Labour, stated in the House of Commons that the negotiations for the settlement of the marine wireless dispute had not so far succeeded. He had refused so far to appoint a Court of Enquiry because the questions at issue were capable of settlement by negotiation. In his view it was still practicable and possible for a settlement to be reached by negotiation, having regard to the extent to which the issues had been narrowed.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: London, Feb. 15.

label: text
text: The "Daily Telegraph"'s diplomatic correspondent says that there is reason to believe that the German Ambassadors and Ministers accredited to the principal League States are being instructed to inform the Governments of those States that the German Government may have to reconsider its position toward the League if the structure of the League Council is modified before Germany has taken a seat on it.

label: text
text:
The “Daily Telegraph’s” Geneva correspondent speaks of the possibility of Germany asking for a postponement of the meeting of the League Assembly fixed for March 8, until the various States have come to an understanding.
Sir Eric Drummond (the League Secretary) has gone to Berlin to discuss the matter with Dr. Stresemann (German Chancellor).

label: text
text: Router learns on high authority that there is no truth whatsoever in the report, circulated abroad, to the effect that Great Britain has agreed to the proposal that permanent sents on the League Council should be awarded to Poland, Spain, and Brazil in addition to Germany.

label: text
text:
More Hedging.
London, Feb. 15.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, in reply to questions, Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, said that a special meeting of the Assembly of the League had been convened for March 8 to consider Germany's application for admission.

label: text
text: Asked whether he could "remove considerable apprehension both here and abroad by stating that the British Government was opposed to any considerable increase

label: text
text: in the Council Sir Austen Chamberlain referred to his reply on the 10th inst. "He said that he gave a considered reply in the hope that he would not be asked other questions until shortly before, he went to Geneva.

label: text
text: Asked whether Germany's application would be considered separately from the applications of other States, Sir Austen Chamberlain said that he was unable to answer for the League in the same specific way as he answered for the Foreign Office.

label: text
text: Technical Questions.

label: text
text: Sir Eric Drummond has arrived from Geneva and had a lengthy conversation with Dr. Strespemann. It is emphasised that Sir Eric Drummond has not come to Berlin to discuss the question of the number of seats on the League Council, which is a matter for the Governments concerned, but to confer with Dr. Strespemann on technical questions in connection with Germany's entry to the League, such as, for example, the ceremony and procedure to be adopted at Geneva when the Assembly meets and Germany's application comes up for consideration.

label: text
text: [Sir Austen Chamberlain in his reply on the 10th inst., said that the application of Germany, as was probably inevitable, had opened the whole question of the composition of the Council. It had led to claims from other quarters, but until it was impossible to reach a final decision as regards the course that would best serve the interests of the Council and the League. He would make a further statement before his departure to attend the Council in March, if possible, but he thought that as a good deal of difference of opinion must at first exist, it would defeat the whole object of the forthcoming meetings and destroy the League's usefulness and influence, if the representatives were bound in advance by rigid instructions which would render a common agreement impossible. The only addition which he was willing to make to the foregoing statement was that more than two other Powers had applied for seats on the Council.]

label: paragraph_title
text: Changes Her Mind

label: text
text:
It is definitely expected that the Countess of Cathcart will withdraw her appeal against exclusion from the United States. It is believed that the publicity provoked by her detention on Ellis Island has caused her to change her mind about the desire to visit America.
The "New York World" says that Lady Craven has confirmed that the Earl is now in Canada where he arrived last evening.

label: text
text:

Washington, Feb. 15.
The Department of Labour has issued a warrant for the Earl of Craven's arrest.

label: text

Montreal, Feb. 15.
The Earl of Craven has arrived here, and is staying at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel. He refused an interview with the Press.

label: text
text: New York, Feb: 15.

label: text
text: The Countess of Cathenæ, looking pale and nervous when interviewed by Pressmen on Ellis Island, declared that she would see the case through. She did not intend under any circumstances to ask permission to return to Britain voluntarily. She had been through a terrible ordeal, but there was a lot of fight left in her yet.

label: text
text:
Montreal, Feb. 15.
The Earl of Craven, in an interview, expressed his surprise to learn that a warrant had been issued against him in the United States. He added that he was glad be on Canadian soil away from the "Land of the Free."

label: text
text: He is sailing from Halifax for Bermuda at the earliest opportunity, whilst his wife will sail from New York for Bermuda on Saturday.

VIEWS

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: A most interesting by-election took place to-day at Belfort where M. Clemenceau's former lieutenant, M. Andre Tardieu, was returned, defeating the Radical Socialist and Communist candidates.

label: text
text: M. Tardieu, who had not returned to public life after his defeat at the General Election in 1924, carried on a whirlwind campaign at Belfort, which was a stronghold of the Left bloc.

label: text
text: M. Tardieu, championed, the malcontents. It is reported that he declared himself opposed to the Locarno Treaties on the ground that they give Britain the control of Europe and push back. Franco from the Rhine.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOCIAL HYGIENE

label: text
text: POSITION IN THE STRAITS SETTLEMENTS.

label: text
text: HOME GOVERNMENT MOVES

label: text
text: London, Feb. 15

label: text
text: Replying to a question as to what action was being taken in connection with the report of the Advisory Committee on Social Hygiene in the Straits Settlements in 1925, Mr. L. S. Amery, Secretary of State for the Colonies said action was being taken on the general lines suggested, notably questions of Immigration of female with male Chinese, in regard to which the Governor of the Straits (Sir Laurence Guillemard) reported that there was already a continued improvement in the sex ratio.

label: text
text:
For many years the questions of housing, education, and recreation had been engaging attention.
The Government did not think that it was necessary to appoint the suggested Mixed Commission, but the medical service was being organised on the lines suggested.
He added that whilst the Straits Government aimed at the disappearance of the brothel, progress must be gradual. Finally, the Government was paying close attention to the recommendation for an increase in the personnel and for an extension of the powers of the Chinese Protectorate.
